Face danger and adventure once more while you search high and low for the most valuable treasures the Caribbean has to offer, then quickly find a safe harbor to stash priceless gold, rare emeralds, and iridescent pearls. Explore, stockpile cargo, hire crew, and commandeer rival ships, but don't forget to bury your loot. As you sail, be on the lookout for a place to settle after your life on the high seas has come to an end, but before you do that, you must outpace your opponents as one trip around the Caribbean won't be enough. You must make three trips in order to retire as the richest and greatest buccaneer of all time. Pirates of Maracaibo is a standalone game in the same franchise as 2019's Maracaibo, and players who are familiar with that game will recognize some beloved concepts from the original. However, new players can jump right in with no prior knowledge of the original game as Pirates of Maracaibo is an independent game with a more accessible rule set. The game plays over three rounds in which you sail the Caribbean, hire crew, ally with other ships, explore the shore, amass the most treasure, and (ideally) retire to a secluded island as the most revered pirate in history. You're a pirate in the Caribbean in this tableau-building game, seeking to hire a versatile crew, grow your hoard of treasure, and improve your pirate ship. Pirates of Maracaibo is played over 3 rounds. Each round, you and your opponents will sail through the Caribbean. You can stop at as many spaces as you want during a round, but watch out! After any player reaches the Maracaibo space, the round will end and all players will move back to the start. What To Do On Your Turn On your turn, you must perform these two steps in this order: Step 1 - Move Your Ship On your turn, you must move 1 to 3 spaces (each card is a space). You may move to any card that is adjacent to your current card, including vertically. You MUST end in a column that is further to the right than where you started. If you end your movement on a card (not the Gulf or Maracaibo) with any opponent Ships, you must pay each of those opponents 1 doubloon. If you do not have enough Doubloons, pay as many players as you can (in the order of your choosing), and ignore the rest. There is no penalty for being unable to pay, so if you are broke, you can move onto a space with other Ships with no consequence! If your ship lands on the Gulf space (to the right of the cards), you must stop there, even if you have extra movement. If you start your turn on the Gulf space, you must move to the Maracaibo space above it. Step 2 - Perform Actions Perform an action based on where your ship landed. [Rating: 1/10] This game is the definition of a soulless and braindead euro. I mean: PIRATES! And what are you doing the whole game? Deliver goods, hire nobles for your ship, help build a cathedral. When you do a fight, you just spend weapons from your track to gain influence in the colonizing powers. Thats it. No fights, no war between ships, no pirate stuff at all. In the category of "how dumb can you implement a topic into a game?" this trash wins it. The game description says: "sail for an adventurous raid". There is not a single raid in this game! You do explicitly NOT raid anything or anyone. Nothing. 

[Rating: 2/10] I hesitate to evaluate this is a shorter/truncated version of MARACAIBO because it plays and progresses much differently. There's not nearly as much tactical or strategic carryover as one might hope, think, or assume. Other than the pace being dictated by the players (a Pfister staple), this has surprising little in common with its older brother. (Honestly, it's very nearly as complex, too, from an efficiency standpoint; the only reason I think it's viewed as a simpler game is because it doesn't have MARACAIBO's massive deck of cards.)
